fact.thing: repeated failure to report income penalty
fact.claim: Trading one crypto-asset for another type of crypto-asset can count as a disposition, so you have to report it on your return. If you leave out $500 or more on your 2025 return and also left out income on your 2022, 2023 or 2024 return, the CRA can charge a penalty. The penalty is whichever is less: 10% of the amount you failed to report (federal and provincial or territorial), or 50% of the understated tax minus any tax withheld on that amount. One missed swap does not trigger it alone, because it only applies to a repeated failure. Budget 2024 said Canada would bring in the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework effective as of 2026, with exchanges of information beginning in 2027, pending legislation.

plain.what: Trading one coin for another — like swapping bitcoin for a different coin — can count as a "disposition" to the CRA. That means Canada's tax office sees it as you giving something up, so it belongs on your tax return, even if no cash ever landed in your bank account. If you leave out $500 or more on your 2025 return and you also left out income on your 2022, 2023 or 2024 return, the CRA can charge a penalty.
plain.so_what: The penalty can be 10% of what you left out, so leaving out $1,000 means up to $100 gone, and one missed swap alone does not trigger it.
plain.do: Pull up your 2022 to 2025 tax returns today and write down any coin swap you left off.
